extra.message: acct_shell_probe_700 builds an OS command by concatenating the user-supplied 'host' GET parameter directly into os.system('ping -c 1 ' + host) with no validation or shell-escaping. An attacker can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. '; rm -rf /' or '$(cmd)') to execute arbitrary commands on the server.

acct_bundle_thaw_184 calls pickle.loads() on raw bytes taken directly from the request body (or a base64-decoded GET parameter). Pickle deserialization of untrusted data allows arbitrary code execution via a crafted __reduce__ payload.

acct_jinja_cast_682 concatenates the user-controlled 'fragment' GET parameter directly into a Jinja2 Template string and renders it: Template('Result: ' + fragment).render(). This is server-side template injection — a request like ?fragment={{ config.__class__... }} or one that reaches __import__ can lead to remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine

extra.message: acct_vault_stash_249 builds a filesystem path from the unsanitized 'ref' GET parameter (target = BASE_EXPORT_DIR / f'{ref}.json') and writes attacker-supplied JSON to it. A value like '../../../../tmp/evil' escapes BASE_EXPORT_DIR, allowing arbitrary file write outside the intended export directory.
acct_vault_stash_249 writes sensitive PII (SSN and full card number, taken directly from request GET parameters) to a plaintext JSON file on disk with no encryption at rest.

cwe: CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information

extra.message: acct_dock_shelf_719 builds a filesystem path directly from the unsanitized 'name' GET parameter (target = BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name) and writes the raw request body to it with write_bytes(). A value like '../../../etc/cron.d/evil' allows writing arbitrary files outside BASE_EXPORT_DIR.

account_return_lane_093 redirects to the user-supplied 'lane' GET parameter with no validation that it is a local/safe URL: return redirect(next_url). An attacker can craft a link to this endpoint that redirects victims to an attacker-controlled domain.

acct_workset_rebind_207 merges the entire client-supplied JSON payload into a privileged state dict with workset.update(payload), letting the caller directly overwrite protected fields such as 'role', 'approved', and 'balance' (e.g. {"role": "admin", "approved": true}).

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: acct_origin_mirror_660 reflects the request's Origin header verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin while also setting Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, allowing any origin to make credentialed cross-site requests and read the response.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: acct_trust_drift_730 creates an SSL context with ssl._create_unverified_context() and uses it for an outbound HTTPS request, disabling certificate/hostname validation and exposing the connection to man-in-the-middle attacks.

acct_badge_gate_690 grants an 'elevated' privilege lane (exposing payroll/casework data) purely based on a client-supplied cookie or header equal to the hardcoded string 'lead', with no server-side session or signature verification. Any client can set this cookie themselves to bypass the intended access control.

cwe: CWE-288: Authentication Bypass Using an Alternate Path or Channel

extra.message: acct_identity_hint_650 checks the user-supplied verifier against a hardcoded credential map ({'north': '4812', 'south': '5930'}) embedded in source code, and returns distinguishable 404 vs 403 responses that let an attacker enumerate valid handles before brute-forcing the 4-digit verifier.

acct_identity_ping_343 is registered under the internal /ops/ console alongside every other partner_console endpoint, but unlike its siblings it never calls _wrk_gate(request), so it is reachable by anyone without the internal ops token.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: account_syncfeed_roll_092 logs the full raw request body and the Authorization header value at WARNING level: logger.warning('deal pipeline intake body=%s auth=%s', wire_text, request.headers.get('authorization')). Credentials and sensitive payload data end up persisted in log files.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: acct_frame_slip_670 explicitly sets X-XSS-Protection to '0' and empties the Content-Security-Policy header on the response, disabling browser-side XSS mitigations for this endpoint.
acct_digest_fold_287 uses MD5 (hashlib.md5) to digest user-supplied 'phrase' data. MD5 is cryptographically broken and unsuitable for any security-sensitive hashing purpose.

cwe: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

extra.message: acct_nonce_roll_710 generates a security-sensitive 'code' using the non-cryptographic random.choice() PRNG instead of the secrets module, making generated codes predictable.

cwe: CWE-330: Use of Insufficiently Random Values

extra.message: account_sheet_glitch_091 reflects the user-supplied 'lot_ref' parameter into a raised exception and returns str(exc) plus the exception class name directly in the JSON error response, leaking internal implementation/path details to the client.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: acct_trace_panel_741 returns the DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE environment variable and the server's internal export base path directly in the JSON response body.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: document_download only checks doc.visibility for support agents (denies only VISIBILITY_BILLING), unlike every other role branch and unlike document_list, which restrict support agents to documents belonging to organizations tied to their assigned escalations via _org_access()/can_access_organization(). A support agent can therefore download any internal or customer-visible document (contracts, security questionnaires, onboarding docs) belonging to ANY organization, not just ones they are assigned to, by simply guessing/enumerating the document UUID.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: SECRET_KEY falls back to a hardcoded, publicly-visible value ('django-insecure-local-dev-only-change-me') when the SECRET_KEY environment variable is not set. If deployed without setting the env var, session signing, password reset tokens, and CSRF protection all rely on a known-in-source secret.

DEBUG defaults to True whenever the DEBUG environment variable is not explicitly set. If this default reaches a production deployment, Django's debug pages expose stack traces, settings values, and source code to any visitor who triggers an exception.

seed_data creates a superuser and other role accounts with hardcoded, weak, guessable passwords ('adminpass123', 'managerpass123', 'supportpass123', 'customerpass123') and prints them to stdout. If this management command is ever run against a shared or production database, these become known privileged credentials.
